title: Palantir Technologies vs. SentinelOne: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Palantir Technologies vs. SentinelOne: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Sara Appino, The Motley Fool
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 2:48 PM EDT 6 min read
PLTR
S
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

As data analysis and security converge, investors face a choice between two high-growth leaders. Should you favor the massive scale of Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) or the specialized agility of SentinelOne (NYSE:S)?

Palantir offers deep data integration for government and commercial giants, while SentinelOne provides AI-driven endpoint protection through a vast partner network. Both companies are capitalizing on the massive shift toward automated intelligence, yet they operate with vastly different financial profiles. This comparison evaluates their growth, profitability, and current market valuations to help you decide which fits your portfolio.

The case for Palantir Technologies

Palantir operates as a powerhouse among tech stocks, specializing in software platforms that integrate and manage massive data sets. The company offers four primary platforms: Gotham, Foundry, Apollo, and the Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP). Its business strategy involves deeply embedding these tools into the operations of government agencies and large commercial enterprises. Palantir maintains long-standing relationships with significant partners, including Stagwell (NASDAQ:STGW), which assists with marketing transformation, and Knox Systems. The company also leverages joint ventures with international partners such as SOMPO Holdings (OTC:NHOLF) and HD Hyundai Co. Ltd. to expand its global footprint.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached nearly $4.5 billion, representing a significant growth of roughly 56.2% year over year. This acceleration was accompanied by strong profitability, as the company reported net income of approximately $1.6 billion. The net margin reached nearly 36.3%, which is a substantial increase from the 16.1% net margin recorded in the prior fiscal year.

According to its December 2025 balance sheet, Palantir maintains a highly liquid financial position with a current ratio of roughly 7.1x. The debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, indicating the company has no total debt relative to its shareholder equity. Free cash flow for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, was close to $2.1 billion, which is calculated as cash from operations minus capital expenditures. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 32% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for SentinelOne

SentinelOne provides AI-powered cybersecurity through its Singularity Platform, which aims to detect and respond to threats across endpoints, cloud workloads, and identities. The company utilizes a channel-led sales model, relying on a vast network of managed service providers and incident response firms for distribution. Key recent partnership expansions include a collaboration with Lenovo to integrate security into their hardware portfolio and an expanded partnership with N-able (NYSE:NABL). This strategy allows the company to reach a broad global audience, including significant operations in Europe and Japan.

Shares of Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) have taken off over the past three months, jumping by an incredible 62% in such a short time amid renewed confidence in software stocks.

The artificial intelligence (AI) software specialist will release its third-quarter results after the market closes on Nov. 2, and I won't be surprised to see Palantir stock get a nice shot in the arm following its report. Let's see why that may be the case.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Palantir can beat expectations once again

Palantir has exceeded Wall Street's earnings expectations impressively in each of the past four quarters. The company's earnings beats have been fueled by strong growth from existing customers, as well as the rapid expansion of the overall customer base.

For instance, Palantir booked $3.37 billion worth of contracts in Q2, an increase of 49% from the year-ago period. Meanwhile, its actual revenue increased by 93% year over year to $1.93 billion. So, Palantir received more contracts than it fulfilled last quarter.

The reason Palantir is landing larger contracts is that customers have been increasing their use of its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) to improve productivity, reduce redundancy, and automate operations using their proprietary data. Notably, Palantir has been able to convert pilot projects and smaller contracts into bigger ones, as management noted on the August earnings call.

As a result, the company's margin profile has been improving at a nice clip. Palantir's adjusted operating margin landed at 62% in Q2, up from 46% in the year-ago period. Not surprisingly, analysts are expecting Palantir's adjusted earnings per share (EPS) to nearly double from the year-ago period in Q2 to $0.41. However, Palantir's adjusted EPS shot up by 2.5x in Q2 from the year-ago period.

Given that the company has been winning more business from existing customers, there is a solid chance its EPS growth could be much stronger than expected. Also, consensus estimates expect Palantir to guide to $0.46 in EPS for the current quarter, a potential jump of 84% over last year. Given that there is still significant room for margin expansion at Palantir, its outlook could exceed expectations.

The stock is unlikely to be held back by its expensive valuation

Shares of Snowflake (SNOW) returned 136.7% from April 28 to October 27, 2026, against 8.8% for the S&P 500. Buyers may be betting that the company's faster sales growth will last, and management ties much of that growth to AI. Sustaining that pace requires two AI products Snowflake built itself to keep winning customers, along with higher customer spending across the core data platform business. So what are those two products, and are customers using them?

What Are Snowflake's Own AI Products Adding?

Management says the latest quarter brought a meaningful step up in AI revenue, and Snowflake's own AI products, Cortex Code and CoWork, are quickly adding customers. Cortex Code reached 5.8 thousand accounts in fiscal Q2 2027, up nearly 11% from the quarter before. Meanwhile, CoWork passed 9.1 thousand accounts, with more than 2,000 added in that quarter alone.

Snowflake's revenue growth accelerated in each of the last three quarters, climbing from 28.7% in fiscal Q3 2026 to 35.1% in fiscal Q2 2027. During the September 2, 2026 call, management said its AI products contributed about half of the acceleration it is seeing, while also naming faster migrations and other products.

Snowflake Says AI Users Spend More Across Its Platform

Customers using AI on Snowflake consume more across the data platform, management said on the same call. That usage would matter for almost the whole company, since product revenue made up 95.5% of Snowflake's total revenue in fiscal 2026. Management also pointed to continued strength in the core data platform business in the second quarter.

It then raised its forecast for fiscal 2027 product revenue to $6.07 billion, or 36% growth, with about 1 point of that growth coming from its Observe acquisition.

Snowflake trades at 21.7 times its last twelve months of sales, against 3.2 times for the S&P 500. The stock closed on October 27 at 8.5% below its highest close of the past year, set on October 9. At 21.7 times sales, buyers are already paying for strong growth to continue.

Where Could Snowflake's AI Push Fall Short?

The AI push could fall short on profit or on staying power, since faster growth does not show what Snowflake earns on AI work or how long new projects last. Management said on the call that it earns a lower contribution margin today on its fast-growing AI workloads. The company still reports a loss, though its operating margin of -17.0% in fiscal Q2 2027 is narrower than -29.7% a year earlier. Management says it is on track for a GAAP profit in fiscal Q4 2028, which is a target, not a result.

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) and Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) are popular artificial intelligence stocks. Since January 2023, Palantir has added 3,000% and Super Micro has advanced 325%. But the Wall Street analysts below think the stocks are overvalued.

Brent Thill at Jefferies recommends selling Palantir. His target price of $80 per share implies 60% downside from its current share price of $199.

Mehdi Hosseini at Susquehanna recommends selling Super Micro. His target price of $15 per share implies 57% downside from the current share price of $35.

Here's what investors should know about these popular AI stocks.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Palantir Technologies: 60% downside implied by Jefferies' target price

Palantir develops data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) platforms to help customers in the public and private sectors integrate data, identify actionable insights, and automate work. Forrester Research recently ranked Palantir as a leader in AI platforms, and Sanjit Singh at Morgan Stanley sees Palantir emerging as the standard in enterprise AI.

The bull case centers around unique software. Whereas traditional analytics tools feature dashboards that tell clients what is happening, Palantir goes further. Its software revolves around a decision-making framework that helps customers decide what should happen next, and it lets them execute actions within the platform.

Palantir is also popular for providing flexibility and supporting privacy. Its AI platform gives customers the freedom to deploy the large language models of their choosing and swap between models without rewriting underlying applications. Palantir's software also includes governance controls that ensure business data is never fed back to model developers.

The bear case for Palantir is entirely focused on its valuation. Despite impressive financial results -- revenue increase 93% in the second quarter, the 12th consecutive acceleration -- Palantir currently trades at 78 times sales, making it the most expensive stock in the S&P 500 by a wide margin. The next closest contender is CrowdStrike at 50 times sales.

Indeed, Brent Thill says Palantir has excellent fundamentals, but the valuation simply does not make sense. He also thinks the company may be underinvesting in future growth, citing its high margins as evidence. But Thill is in the minority on Wall Street, as most analysts think the stock is undervalued. Palantir has a median target price of $223 per share, implying 12% upside from its current share price of $199.

What Happened?

General Motors (GM:NYSE) said on Tuesday it will move its stock listing to Nasdaq from the New York Stock Exchange, and the stock rose about 5.5% on the news.

GM expects to start trading on Nasdaq on November 17, and will keep its current ticker symbol. It will also become the first legacy automaker on the exchange.

GM is not the first big name to make the switch, as Walmart, Hilton and Palantir have moved recently too. Reuters says these companies want to be closer to tech stocks as investors chase the AI buildout.

CFO Paul Jacobson said GM's technology-driven strategy is creating value for stockholders and called Nasdaq "a natural home" for the listing.

GM Stock Revenue, EBIT and Free Cash Flow Estimates in Billion USD (TIKR)

GM is putting money into new technology, which includes "eyes-off" self-driving on some models. It is also building a new software base for future vehicles, and the goal is to get drivers to pay for digital features.

What the Market Is Telling Us About General Motors Stock

A listing change does not alter how GM makes money, but it shows how the company wants to be seen. General Motors stock is being pitched as a tech-driven story, not just a car maker.

The business gives that pitch some support. In Q3, revenue hit a record $50 billion and adjusted earnings per share rose more than 30% to $3.70. OnStar Digital and Super Cruise brought in over $800 million in recognized revenue, up 15%.

GM also keeps buying back shares and announced a new $20 billion buyback authorization, more than 25% of its current market value, according to management.

For General Motors stock, buybacks shrink the share count and help lift earnings per share.

There are risks. Management said commodity, shipping, and memory costs add about $2 billion in headwinds this year.

It also said 2027 could be harder if those costs stay high.

2.      Apollo: Manages the secure deployment and continuous updating of software across diverse environments, providing a unified control layer for delivering new features, security updates, and platform configurations.

3.      Foundry: A central operating system for enterprise data, allowing users to integrate, organize, and analyze information in a single environment to support business operations and decision-making.

4.      AIP: Enables organizations to integrate large language models and other AI technologies into operational workflows.

Government Demand Drives Palantir's Growth

Palantir has a major advantage over most AI companies because it mainly sells its software to deep-pocketed, sticky commercial and government customers. Additionally, Palantir is insulated from competition because it has been earned FedRAMP High and Department of Defense Impact Level 6 accreditations, the highest security clearances required for sensitive national security and defense intelligence systems. In Q2, U.S. commercial and government revenues soared 149% and 90% respectively, while Palantir closed 220 deals worth at least $1 million (including 73 worth at least $10 million).

Palantir: A Hedge on Global Turmoil

While most tech companies are adversely impacted by geopolitical turmoil, Palantir benefits from it. US. Defense spending has soared in recent years, and with no resolution in sight to two major wars, Palantir acts as a valuable geopolitical hedge for Wall Street investors.

Palantir: Low Capex Spend

Unlike most leading AI companies, Palantir's annual Capex spending is tepid. Palantir can do this because instead of investing in capital-heavy data centers, it builds the application layer of the AI ecosystem. Assuming the current run rate persists, the company is expected to spend under $50 million in Capex for full-year 2026.
